77297.subject: Agricultural Science
77297.question_text:
(a) Identify specimens A, B and C

(b) Give one function of each of Specimen A, B and C

(c) State two ways of maintaining each of specimen A and B

(d) Name three other farm implements that perform the same function as specimen B

(e) Mention two precautions to be observed when using specimen B
77297.explanation:
(a) A - Nut and bolt;
B - Knapsack sprayer;
C - Identification tag.

(b) A is used in tightening, fastening, fixing or holding joints together.
B is used for spraying or applying fungicides, insecticides.
-is used for spraying liquid fertilizers.
-is used for spraying herbicides.
C is used for identification of animals.

(c)  Ways of maintaining specimen A:
-Grease to avoid rusting.
-Straighten bent bolt or nut.
-Rethreading the worn-out threads.
-Store always in cool, dry place.
Ways of maintaining specimen B
-Wash and clean the tank, the filters and nozzles with water after use.
-Check the sprayer for leakage and any leakage should be blocked.
-Replace damage or worn-out parts, e.g., filters and nozzles.
-Remove the nozzles, clean and store seperately.
-Store the sprayer under cover.
-Free the nozzles of all blockages or clogs.
-Turn the container upside down after washing to drain properly.

(d) -Motorized sprayer
-Boom sprayer
-Electrotyne sprayer
-Hand sprayer

(e) -Wear protective clothing and a nose mask.
-Avoid eating. drinking or smoking.
-Wash/bath well after spraying.
-Do not blow a blocked nozzle with the mouth.
-Ensure that spraying is not against the wind.
-Avoid walking on freshly sprayed plots.
-Follow carefully instructions on the use of chemical to be sprayed

77298.subject: Agricultural Science
77298.question_text:
(a) To what type of rock do each of specimens D, E, and F belong?

(b) State the types of weathering caused by each of specimens G, H, and 1

(c) Give two ways by which weathering causes each of specimens G, H, and I.

(d) State three ways in which specimen D is important to agriculture
77298.explanation:
(a) (i) D is an igneous rock
(ii) E is a sedimentary rock
(ii) F is an igneous rock

(b) Specimen G (Earthworm) - Physical/mechanical
Specimen H (Water) - Physical and Chemical
Specimen I (Ice Block) - Physical / mechanical

(c) Specimen G burrows into rocks and creates wide cleavages which cause rocks to disintergrate into smaller particles and
this creates room for water and air which aid rock disintegration.
Specimen H dissolves to form weak acids that dissolve rock particles and attaches H and OH ions to some compounds to
form minerals. Running water drags rock particles along and these collide with themselves and wall and thus breakdown.
The force of running water pulls away rock particles from embankments/floor of channels.
Specimen I - conversion of water into ice results in increase in Volume and pressure exerted within the rock causes it to
crack and fall apart. Also movement of ice along a path leads to further dislodgement of particles.

(d) -It forms soil when weathered.
-It serves as a source of soil nutrients/elements.
-It can be pilled up and used to check erosion.
-It can be used to construct farm structures.
-It can also be used to construct access roads.
-It can also damage tools when in use.

77309.subject: Agricultural Science
77309.question_text:
(a) State each of the disease condition observed on specimens J (MAIZE PLANT) and K (CASSAVA LEAF) and their causative agents.

(b) Explain the mode of transmission of the diseases on each of specimens J and K.

(c) State two effects each of the diseases on Specimens J and K and two control measures of each

(d) Name two other diseases of specimen K.
77309.explanation:
(a) Specimen J is maize plant with leaves showing a mosaic pattern/infection, tomato plant, showing leaf curl.
The causative agent for this Condition is virus.
Specimen K is cassava leaf, showing leaf spot.
The causative agent is fungus.

(b) For specimen J, the virus is transmitted by an aphid vector.
For specimen K, the fungus is air- borne, water and rain splash

(c) Specimen J (effects):
-It results in stunted growth of plants.
-It leads to reduction in yield of plants.
-It causes reduction in the photosynthetic area of the leaf.
Control measures include:
-early planting:

Control measures include:
-application of fungicides,
-use of resistant varieties,
-removal and burning of infected plants, and
-crop rotation.
-removal and burning of infected plants;
-eradication of insect vectors;
-use of resistant varieties; and
-crop rotation
For specimen K (effects);
-It causes reduction in yield of crop or plant.
-It leads to the reduction in the rate of growth of plants.
-It also leads to reduction in the photosynthetic area of the leaves.

(d) Other diseases of specimen K are;
-Cassava mosaic
-Cassava blight

77386.subject: Agricultural Science
77386.question_text:
(a) ldentify specimens L, M and N

(b) ldentify specimens O and P, using specimen N

(c) In which of specimens O and P will specimen M survive better?

(d) What is the relevance of specimen L in the production of specimen M?

(e) State two pond management practices to improve specimen O for the production of specimen M.

(f) List three ways by which the loss of specimen M can be controlled in a farm.

(gi) State one method each of partial harvesting of specimen M.

(gii) State one method each of complete harvesting of specimen M.
77386.explanation:
(a) Specimen L is NPK Fertilizer
Specimen M is Tilapia Fish
Specimen N is Litmus Paper

(b) Litmus paper test shows that specimen O is acidic while P is neutral
Acidic liquid (Fluid)
Neutral liquid (Distilled water) 

(c) Specimen M will survive better in P

(d) Specimen L is used to fertilize a fish pond in small quantities to provide nutrients for the growth of phytoplanktons
which are eaten by fish

(e) Pond management practises to improve specimen O for the production of specimen M includes:
desilting.
liming
fertilizer application

(f) Ways by which the loss of specimen M can be controlled in a farm are;
-Control gate to prevent excess out of flow of water from dam
-Errection of spill-way.
-Maintaining patrol to prevent stealing.
-Control of predators.,
Control of diseases.
Avoid over flooding by erecting barriers across flood part

(gi) Partial harvesting of specimen O can be achieved through the use of;

-Hook and line
-Traps,
-Baskets,
-Net and spears

(gii) Method of complete harvesting of specimen O is by drainage of the pond,
